The key represents the priority and the value  is the public key algorithm to be configured at that priority  level. No configuration here means that the default public key  algorithms and priorities will be configured:   1.  rsa-sha2-256   2.  rsa-sha2-512   3.  ssh-rsa   4.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp256   5.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp384   6.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp521   7.  ssh-ed25519   8.  x509v3-rsa2048-sha256   9.  x509v3-ssh-rsa   10. x509v3-sign-rsa   11. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256   12. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp384   13. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp521

ssh_publickeyauthentication_enable.description: Controls whether ssh public key authentication is enabled. This value will not be honored if two-factor authentication is enabled.

ssh_server_allowlist_enable.description: Controls whether the ssh server allow-list is enabled. When enabled, only configured hosts can connect to SSH servers of the switch.

ssh_server_allowlist_ips.description: Custom ssh server allow-list containing configured IPv4s and IPv6s.

ssh_server_port.description: Server port for all SSH servers on all VRFs where ssh server is  enabled.

ssh_twofactorauthentication_enable.description: This column can have one of the following settings: 'password': This means that authentication can only succeed with             successful certificate and password authentication. 'radius-authorize-only': This setting means that authentication                   will be done with a certificate followed by an                   authorization request to a RADIUS server 'disabled': Neither of the above configurations are enabled.

stp_config.description: This represents information regarding stp global configuration.

bpdu_guard_timeout.description: Time in seconds until when a port configured for BPDU-guard will be disabled upon receiving an STP BPDU. If bpdu_guard_timeout is not set, port will be in the disabled state forever.

extended_sysid_disable.description: System ID is kept as zero in the Bridge ID if this value is 'true'

forward_delay.description: The forward delay time in seconds for all the instances.

hello_time.description: The hello time in seconds for all the instances.

ignore_pvid_inconsistency_enable.description: Ignores PVID inconsistencies and allow RPVST to run on mismatched links if this value if 'true'.

max_age.description: The maximum-aging time in seconds (The time a device waits without receiving spanning tree configuration messages before attempting a reconfiguration) for all the instances.

max_hop_count.description: The maximum hop count for all the instances.

mstp_config_name.description: The MSTP configuration name configured by user. Default value is system MAC address.

mstp_config_revision.description: The MSTP configuration revision number configured by user.

path_cost_type.description: The operational value of the path cost type either long or short.

priority.description: The priority value configured as a multiple of 4096 The lower a priority value, the higher the priority.

rpvst_mstp_interconnect_vlan.description: VLAN used to interconnect an RPVST domain to an MSTP domain. This is only applicable if spanning tree is enabled on this device and the mode is set to RPVST.

stp_enable.description: Global knob to enable or disable Spanning Tree Protocol. Spanning Tree Protocol is enabled if this value is 'True'.

stp_mode.description: Spanning tree mode. The possible spanning tree modes are mstp  - Specify spanning tree to run in MSTP mode. rpvst - Specify spanning tree to run in Rapid PVST mode

tx_hold_count.description: The value used by the STP transmit state machine to limit the maximum transmission rate of BPDUs within the hello interval.

target.description: URL of the TFTP server to which supportlogs will be sent.  URL format: 'tftp://{IP|HOST}[:PORT][;blocksize=VAL]/FOLDER/'.

supportlog_rotate_vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
VRF over which the remote TFTP server (to transfer supportlogs) is to be reached. If not specified, default VRF is used. This column value can be empty.

syslog_audit_format_native.description: Enable sending audit log messages to the syslog server in Linux format. If it is not enabled, then it sends in ArubaOS-CX defined log format.

syslog_remote_facility.description: Facility to be used when forwarding to remote syslog servers.

syslog_remotes.description:
Reference Resource: [Syslog_Remote](#/Syslog_Remote)
List of syslog servers to which syslog messages will be forwarded. [Syslog_Remote](#/Syslog_Remote)

tcp_synack_retries.description: Number of times SYN-ACK packets are resent in response to a TCP  SYN request.

threshold_profile_default.description:
Reference Resource: [Threshold_Profile](#/Threshold_Profile)
Specifies the threshold-profile name for ports that do not specify their own profile (see [Port](#/Port) threshold_profile column).

timezone.description: User configured Timezone. Time zone of the device in case sensitive Posix format - "US/Pacific","Asia/Singapore", "Etc/GMT". Please refer to the full list of supported time zones at `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones`.

tls_certified_algorithms_only.description: Specifies whether TLS crypto algorithms should be restricted to  only those algorithms certified to Common Criteria NDcPP requirements.

tls_check_key_usage.description: enable the key usage check on a peer cert received during TLS handshake for client-auth or server-auth usage.

trunk_dynamic_vlan_include.description: Set to enable or disable a trunk port from automatically transmitting or receiving traffic for dynamic VLANs i.e., MVRP and PortAccess VLANs.

ubt_client_vid.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
VLAN-ID assigned to clients whose traffic is being redirected to the UBT cluster. This is not set when the UBT mode is set to VLAN-extend.

ubt_mode.description: UBT VLAN mode configuration:  `vlan-extend`: Clients are assigned to their UBT-role based                 VLAN in the hardware datapath. This mode allows                 for UBT to support VLAN-tagged clients like VOIP                 phones.  `local-vlan` : Clients are assigned to a VLAN that is local to                 the switch and associated with their UBT-role                 based VLAN when client traffic reaches the                 controller. This mode allows for reducing the                 number of VLANs that need to be instantiated on                 the switch but can only support VLAN-untagged UBT                 clients. The 'ubt_client_vid' will be used to                 specify the local_vlan that UBT clients are                 assigned to.

unicast_gr_disabled.description: The unicast_gr_disabled flag is used to indentify whether the Unicast GR feature enabled or not

usb_disable.description: Disable USB port. When disabled, devices inserted into the  USB port of the switch will not be detected and will not work.

virtual_mac.description: Global virtual MAC configuration. An example usage would be  EVPN Symmetric IRB where EVPN advertises this MAC as the Router's MAC for all the EVPN Symmetric Routes.

vlan_client_presence_detect.description: If enabled, VNI mapped VLANs will be 'UP' only if there are authenticated clients on this VLAN or have some statically configured ports as members and those ports are 'UP'. When not set, VNI mapped VLANs will always be 'UP'.

vsx.description:
Reference Resource: [VSX](#/VSX)
VSX configuration and status. If not configured, VSX functionality is disabled.

vsx_trap_enable.description: Enables sending SNMP traps for VSX events.

ztp_force_provision.description: Force ZTP based provisioning to run, ignoring the status of any previous ZTP operation.

accounting_fail_through.description: This determines whether to access the next remote AAA server in case accounting is not recorded with the current server, the accounting will be attempted with the next configured server. If true, the next server in line will be accessed. If false, accounting will not be attempted with the next server.

authorization_fail_through.description: This determines whether to access the next remote AAA server in case of failure with the current server, the authorization will be attempted with the next configured server. If true, the next server in line will be accessed. If false, authorization will not be attempted with the next server.

console_lockout_time.description: Lock out time (in seconds) of user for console access after the failure for the number of attempts mentioned in failed console login attempts. This value will not be honored if RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication is enabled.

console_login_attempts.description: Maximum failed console login attempts. If no value is set, the default is no limit on console login attempts. This value will not be honored if RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication is enabled.

dot1x_radius_server_group.description: RADIUS server group to use for 802.1x authentication.

dot1x_remote_auth_method.description: Remote authentication method to be used by  the 802.1x authenticator: `eap-radius`:  extensible authentication protocol.

eap_tls_fragment_size_towards_server.description: Maximum size in bytes of an EAP-TLS fragment encoded in a  single RADIUS request packet.

fail_through.description: This determines whether to access the next remote AAA server in case of an authentication failure from the current one If true, the next server in line will be accessed. If false, the authentication process will be aborted at the first instance of an authentication failure.

login_lockout_time.description: Length (in seconds) of user lockout after too many failed login attempts. This value has no effect unless max login attempts is set. This value will not be honored if RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication is enabled.

mac_auth_address_format.description: The MAC address format to be used in the RADIUS request messages  for MAC authentication.  `no-delimiter`            : aabbccddeeff  `single-dash`             : aabbcc-ddeeff  `multi-dash`              : aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-ff  `multi-colon`             : aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff  `no-delimiter-uppercase`  : AABBCCDDEEFF  `single-dash-uppercase`   : AABBCC-DDEEFF  `multi-dash-uppercase`    : AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF  `multi-colon-uppercase`   : AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.

mac_auth_password.description: The password to be used for MAC authentication in  the RADIUS request messages.

mac_auth_radius_auth_method.description: The type of Radius authentication method to use for MAC authentication: `CHAP`: challenge-handshake authentication protocol over RADIUS. `PAP`:  password authentication protocol over RADIUS.

mac_auth_radius_server_group.description: RADIUS server group to use for MAC authentication.

max_login_attempts.description: Maximum failed login attempts. If no value is set, the default is no limit on login attempts. This value will not be honored if RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication is enabled.

portaccess_accounting_radius_server_grou.description: RADIUS server group that this device will send accounting updates to.

portaccess_local_accounting_enable.description: Enables local accounting for portaccess clients in the system.

privilege_elevation.description: Indicates whether the privilege elevation method is enabled for login access to the switch for adminstrator users.

radius_auth.description: Specifies encoding to be used for the user password for radius based authentication.

radius_dns_query_interval.description: Specifies the interval, in seconds, between DNS requests sent from the switch to the DNS server to resolve the RADIUS FQDN address. This is only applicable when `radius_dns_query_mode` is set to 'fixed'.

radius_dns_query_mode.description: Specifies the DNS query mode.  `backoff`: The DNS interval is determined by an exponential             backoff algorithm. The query interval starts at             1 second and is doubled after every 20 unsuccessful             retries until the interval reaches 60 seconds.             i.e., the query intervals would be 1, 2, 4, 8,             16, 32, 60 with 20 attempts at each interval until             it reaches 60.  `fixed`:   The DNS query is sent at a fixed interval defined             in `radius_dns_query_interval`.

radius_dns_refresh_interval.description: Specifies the time interval in seconds to wait before the switch refreshes its DNS cache for RADIUS servers and Dynamic authorization clients configured with a FQDN address.

radius_passkey.description: Specifies the shared secret key between the RADIUS client and the RADIUS server.

radius_retries.description: Specifies the number of retries to radius server if there is no response.

radius_service_type_in_access_req.description: Specifies if the Service-Type attribute must be included  in RADIUS Access-Request packets.

radius_timeout.description: Specifies the timeout interval in seconds that the switch waits for response from the RADIUS server before declaring a timeout failure.

radius_tls_initial_connection_timeout.description: RADIUS over TLS initial connection timeout in seconds.

radius_tls_timeout.description: RADIUS over TLS server response timeout in seconds.

radius_tracking_max_retries.description: Specifies the Maximum number of requests to be sent for tracking on retry. If not specified, then 'radius_retries' will be used.

radius_tracking_password.description: Specifies the password to be passed in the Access-Request packet for RADIUS server tracking.

radius_tracking_time_interval.description: Specifies the time interval in seconds between the status requests to the server.

radius_tracking_user_name.description: Specifies the user name to be passed in the Access-Request packet for RADIUS server tracking.

status_server_message_interval.description: Specifies the time interval in seconds between consecutive status messages sent to the server.

tacacs_auth.description: Specifies encoding to be used for the user password for tacacs+ authentication.

tacacs_passkey.description: Specifies the shared secret key between the TACACS+ client and the TACACS+ server.

tacacs_single_connection_disable.description: Disable single-connection mode between switch and TACACS+ server.

tacacs_timeout.description: Specifies the timeout interval in seconds that the switch waits for response from the TACACS+ server before declaring a timeout failure.

tacacs_tracking_password.description: Specifies the password to be used in the authentication START packet for TACACS+ server tracking.

tacacs_tracking_time_interval.description: Specifies the time interval in seconds between the status requests to the server.

tacacs_tracking_user_name.description: Specifies the user name to be used in the authentication START packet for TACACS+ server tracking.

all_user_copp_policies.description:
Reference Resource: [CoPP_Policy](#/CoPP_Policy)
List of all user-defined CoPP policies in the system. The existence of a policy in this list is not an indication that it has been applied.

timeout.description: ARP aging timeout in seconds. Defines how many seconds a MAC address remains active in the MAC address table.

bfd_detect_multiplier.description: The number of negotiated min_rx_intervals that can occur before a BFD session is considered to be down.

bfd_enable.description: Specifies whether the BFD protocol is enabled or not on the system.

bfd_min_echo_rx_interval.description: The shortest interval, in milliseconds, at which BFD sessions can receive BFD control messages. Remote endpoints may send messages at a slower rate. The value 0 means that the system does not want to receive BFD echo packets. The range from [1-49] is invalid.

bfd_min_rx_interval.description: The shortest interval, in milliseconds, at which BFD sessions can receive BFD control messages. Remote endpoints may send messages at a slower rate.

bfd_min_tx_interval.description: The shortest interval, in milliseconds, at which BFD sessions can transmit BFD control messages. Messages will actually be transmitted at a slower rate if the remote endpoints cannot receive them as quickly as specified.

bluetooth_mgmt_disable.description: Disables Bluetooth management. When disabled, Bluetooth adapters  inserted into the USB port of the switch will not be detected  and will not work. If the USB port is disabled via usb_disable,  then this setting will have no effect.

cdp_mode.description: Sets CDP mode globally on the system: 'enable':               Enables CDP globally 'disable':              Disables CDP globally 'pass_through_enable':  CDP packet will be forwarded through multicast forwarding

certificate_association.description: Names of the certificates to be used for supported applications.  If the name is not valid or the certificate is corrupted /  expired, a default self-signed certificate will be used instead.

disable.description: Disables checkpointing after bursts of configurations.

timeout.description: Number of seconds that the system will wait after burst of configurations and before creating a post-config checkpoint.

acl_secure_update.description: Specifies whether traffic is blocked to ensure security during ACL update operations.

timeout.description: The maximum allowed idle time, in minutes, after  which a CLI session will be terminated. Value of 0  disables the timeout.

tracking_range.description: The maximum time period, in days, for which a user's  login sessions will be tracked.

enable.description: Enable client on-boarding related insight collection. 'true' : enables client insight configuration globally. 'false': disables client insight configuration on the system.

log_onboard_events.description: Specifies whether on-boarding event logs are enabled for clients. For  on-boarding event logs to work, client insight feature should be  enabled before. 'true' : enables on-boarding event logs for clients. 'false': disables on-boarding event logs for clients.

configuration_lockout_config.description: Configure the system to be managed by a remote NMS. Every entry represents an owner and its corresponding configuration mode. This helps the external manager identify whether or not the device's configuration can be changed by anyone else.

central.description: When set to `managed`, this indicates that Central has requested for an exclusive 'write' access to the device configuration.

configured_profile.description: Profile that the system should use. If not set, the system boots with the default profile, as specified in the available_profiles. Note that for any change to take effect, the system must be restarted.

console_baudrate.description: Set the console serial port data transmission speed.

enable.description: Specifies whether console-logging feature is enabled.

filter_regex.description: Specifies the POSIX regular expression filter associated with console-logging.

log_type.description: Specifies the type of log notification.

cpu_trap_disable.description: Disable SNMP trap generation for the CPU utilization alert.

broadcast-flag.description: Set broadcast flag in DHCP request packets

host_name.description: Include host-name-option in DHCP request packets.

relay_l2vpn_clients.description: Enable DHCP-Relay functionality for remote l2 VPN clients.

v4relay_disabled.description: Set this value to `true` to disable DHCP-Relay functionality globally and set it to `false` to enable it. DHCP-Relay is enabled by default. If the key is missing, the configuration is assumed to be enabled. Though DHCP-Relay configuration is enabled globally, the functionality is effective only after the port level server configuration.

v4relay_hop_count_increment_disabled.description: Set this value to `true` to disable the hop count increment in the relayed DHCP requests and set it to `false` otherwise. This configuration is enabled by default. If the key is missing, the configuration is assumed to be enabled.

v4relay_option82_enabled.description: Set this value to `true` to enable the DHCP-Relay Option 82 and set it to `false` otherwise. This configuration is disabled by default. If the key is missing, the configuration is assumed to be disabled.

v4relay_option82_policy.description: Specifies the forwarding policy of DHCP-Relay Option 82.  `drop` - Drop an inbound dhcp-client request with an Option 82 field already appended. If no Option 82 fields are present, drop causes the router to add an Option 82 field to dhcp request and forward.  `keep` - If the relay agent receives a client request that already has one or more Option 82 fields, keep causes the relay agent to retain such fields and forward the request without adding another Option 82 field. But if the incoming client request does not already have any Option 82 fields, the relay agent appends an Option 82 field and forwards the dhcp request.  `replace` - Replace any existing Option 82 fields from downstream relay agents (and/or the originating client) with an Option 82 field for the current relay agent.  If the keys is missing, Option 82 configuration is assumed to be disabled.

v4relay_option82_remote_id.description: Specifies the remote ID suboption that the switch uses in Option 82 fields added or appended to DHCP client packets. The type of remote ID defines DHCP policy areas in the client requests sent to the DHCP server.  `ip` - Specifies the IP address of the interface on which the client DHCP packet enters the switch.  `mac` - Specifies the router's MAC address. (The MAC address used is the same MAC address that is assigned to all interfaces configured on the routing switch.)  If the key is not specified, configuration is assumed to be "mac".

v4relay_option82_validation_enabled.description: Set this value to `true` to validate server response packets and set it to `false` otherwise. This configuration is disabled by default. If the key is missing, the configuration is assumed to be disabled. This configuration is valid only for drop or replace dhcp-relay Option 82 policy.

v4relay_reply_overwrite_source_ip_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable DHCP-Relay Reply Overwrite Source IP functionality  in the DHCP Reply packets from the DHCP server, globally and set it to `false`  otherwise. The configuration is disabled by default. If the key is missing,  the configuration is assumed to be disabled.

v4relay_source_interface_enabled.description: Set the value to 'true' to enable DHCP-Relay to use the  configured source-interface and include suboption-5 and  suboption-11 in the relay option 82.

v4smartrelay_enabled.description: Set this value to `true` to enable DHCP-Smart-Relay functionality globally and  set it to `false` otherwise. The functionality is effective only after  DHCP-Relay is enabled globally and at the interface level.

v6relay_enabled.description: Set this value to `true` to enable DHCPv6-Relay functionality globally and set it to `false` to disable it. This configuration is disabled by default. Though DHCPv6-Relay configuration is enabled globally, the functionality is effective only after the port level server configuration.

v6relay_l2vpn_clients.description: Enable DHCPv6-Relay functionality for remote l2 VPN clients.

v6relay_option79_enabled.description: Set this value to `true` to enable the DHCPv6-Relay Option 79 and set it to `false` otherwise. This configuration is disabled by default.

v6relay_source_interface_enabled.description: Set the value to 'true' to enable DHCPv6-Relay to use the  configured source-interface and include option-68.

dhcp_server_external_storage.description:
Reference Resource: [External_Storage](#/External_Storage)
External storage to be used for all DHCPv4 servers.

delay.description: Interval between lease file updates in seconds.

lease_file.description: File to store DHCPv4 lease information. If not specified then a default file by name `dhcpv4-leases` prefixed with the configured hostname or system MAC will be used.

dhcpv4_snooping_external_storage.description:
Reference Resource: [External_Storage](#/External_Storage)
External storage to back up IP bindings learnt by DHCPv4 snooping.

file_name.description: File to store IP bindings learnt by DHCPv4 snooping. If not specified then a default file by name `ip-bindings` prefixed with the configured hostname or system MAC will be used.

allow_overwrite_binding.description: Allows binding to be overwritten for the same IP address. When set, existing IP binding entry is overwritten if DHCP server assigns  same IP address to a different client. When not set, such DHCP offers are dropped.

disable_mac_verification.description: Disables MAC address validation on DHCP packets. When not set, DHCP packets on untrusted ports with different DHCP client  hardware address and packet source MAC address are dropped.

enable.description: Enables DHCPv4 snooping across the system.

enable_client_attribute_caching.description: Enables storing static attributes provided to DHCP-client by DHCP-Server during DHCP packet exchange. When enabled, following attributes are stored in client IP Binding entry: 1. DNS servers 2. Router IPs 3. Server IP

vxlan_trusted.description: Enable DHCPv4 snooping trust attribute on VxLAN tunnel interfaces.

disable.description: If not disabled, DHCP snooping adds DHCP relay information option to DHCP client packets that it forwards on trusted ports, and examins/strips the preexisting relay information on untrusted ports. When disabled, DHCPv4 snooping doesn't add or process DHCP relay information option.

remote_id.description: The value that will be used for the remote ID sub-option of the relay  information that will be inserted by DHCP snooping:  'mac':      switch MAC address 'subnetIP': switch IP address on the VLAN on which the DHCP packet was received 'mgmtIP':   switch IP address on the management interface.

untrusted_policy.description: The behavior of DHCP when forwarding a DHCP packet from an untrusted port that already has a DHCP relay information option present.  The supported policies are: 'keep':    forward the packet without updating the existing option 'replace': replace the existing option with the one generated by this switch 'drop':    drop the packet

dhcpv6_server_external_storage.description:
Reference Resource: [External_Storage](#/External_Storage)
External storage to be used for all DHCPv6 servers.

delay.description: Interval between lease file updates in seconds.

lease_file.description: File to store DHCPv6 lease information. If not specified then a default file by name `dhcpv6-leases` prefixed with the configured hostname or system MAC will be used.

dhcpv6_snooping_external_storage.description:
Reference Resource: [External_Storage](#/External_Storage)
External storage to back up IPv6 bindings learnt by DHCPv6 snooping.

file_name.description: File to store IPv6 bindings learnt by DHCPv6 snooping. If not specified then a default file by name `ipv6-bindings` prefixed with the configured hostname or system MAC will be used.

enable.description: Enables DHCPv6 snooping across the system.

vxlan_trusted.description: Enable DHCPv6 snooping trust attribute on VxLAN tunnel interfaces.

dlog_destination.description: Filter the dlogs that are sent to each possible destination based on the severity specified. If a destination is not present, no dlog messages will be sent to that destination. If no destinations are present then dlogs of severity debug or greater will be sent to buffer. Example: {'file':'info'} info and above level dlogs will be send to file destination.

domain_name.description: Domain name as configured by the user.

download_data_limit.description: The file download data limit per hour in GB.

delay.description: Interval between lease file updates in seconds. File update occurs only if there is a change in the client IP bindings.

enable.description: Enables local storage in DHCPv4 Snooping.

delay.description: Interval between lease file updates in seconds. File update occurs only if there is a change in the client IP bindings.

enable.description: Enables local storage in DHCPv6 Snooping.

dynamic_mode.description: flow_based - Enable flow based dynamic load balancing.              Packets of a unique flows are assigned to              an ECMP member while they remain active.              New flows are assigned to an ECMP member              with smallest ECMP member link bandwidth              utilization. packet_based - Enable packet based dynamic load                balancing. Every ingress packet to an                ECMP group will get ECMP member                assignment based on link bandwidth                utilization.

dynamic_mode_context.description: outer-header - Dynamic mode ECMP is applicable only if                there are multiple equal cost paths                available for routing the                outer header of the packet. In case of                tunnel encapsulation, if there are multiple                equal cost path available for routing the                inner packet, the destination chosen for                the inner header will not be dynamically                load balanced.

dynamic_mode_flow_based_inactivity_timeo.description: If there is no ingress packet belonging to a flow during the inactivity timeout duration in (us), flow would be considered a new flow for flow based dynamic load balancing.

enabled.description: Determines whether ECMP is enabled in the system. Default is true.

hash_dstip_enabled.description: Determines whether destination IP participates in ECMP hash calculation. Default is true.

hash_dstport_enabled.description: Determines whether destination TCP/UDP port participates in ECMP hash calculation. Default is true.

hash_srcip_enabled.description: Determines whether source IP participates in ECMP hash calculation. Default is true.

hash_srcport_enabled.description: Determines whether source TCP/UDP port participates in ECMP hash calculation. Default is true.

resilient_hash_enabled.description: Determines whether ECMP hashing preserves traffic flows when ECMP group membership changes. Default is true.

enable_snmpv3_only.description: Enables only the SNMPv3 mode of operation and disallows SNMP v1 and v2c.

entityd_trap_disable.description: Enable SNMP trap generation for Entity MIB related events.

event_trap_disable.description: Disable SNMP trap generation for event logs.

forwarding_mode_config.description: The packet forwarding mode to use for all ports in the system.   `store-and-forward` - packets are received and queued before forwarding `cut-through` - packets can begin transmission while still being received

global_user_copp_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [CoPP_Policy](#/CoPP_Policy)
Specifies the user-configured top-level CoPP policy. When missing, the policy in the [hw_default_copp_policy](#/System) column will be used.

hostname.description: Host name as configured by the user.

hpe_rda_enable.description: Specify to `true` to enable Remote Device Access to the switch.

http_proxy_location_vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
VRF for HTTP Proxy connections. If not set, then the 'default' VRF will be used.

max_per_user.description: Maximum number of concurrent sessions per user.  *Note*: The maximum number of sessions may impact the system performance because of the number of concurrent request coming from the clients. Be cautious with the value configured here.

timeout.description: The maximum idle time for an HTTPS session in minutes. A value of 0 disables the timeout. The HTTPS session can  still be terminated by the absolute timeout (8 hours)  regardless of activity.

icmp_redirect_disable.description: Disable ICMPv4 and ICMPv6 redirect messages.

icmp_throttle.description: ICMP throttle (in seconds) can be used to configure the  packet interval to send ICMPv4/v6 error and redirect messages.

icmp_unreachable_disable.description: Disable ICMPv4 and ICMPv6 unreachable messages.

igmp_global_snooping.description: Enable/Disable the IGMP Snooping Functionality globally.

ipv6_hop_limit.description: Maximum number of hops, after which packets originating from the switch will be discarded.

ipv6_route_gc_interval.description: Garbage collection interval timer in seconds. Once the timer expires,  the invalid or old entries will be removed from kernel route cache.

isp_allow_non_failsafe_updates_config_du.description: The number of minutes configured by the user for which non-failsafe updates are allowed.

lacp-system-id.description: The LACP system ID of this [Bridge](Bridge).  The system ID of a LACP bond is used to identify itself to its partners.  Must be a nonzero MAC address. Defaults to the bridge Ethernet address if unset.

lacp-system-priority.description: The LACP system priority of this [Bridge](Bridge).  In LACP negotiations, link status decisions are made by the system with the numerically lower priority. Defaults to 65534.

log_notification_threshold.description: Set the threshold percentage relative to the size of the log buffer. Once the utilization  has reached this threshold, a log notification will be generated.

logging_filter.description:
Reference Resource: [Logging_Filter](#/Logging_Filter)
Currently active logging filter.This column value can be empty.

enable.description: Enable logging to persistent storage for the specified duration.

filter.description: Enable logging to the persistant storage for specified filter.

max_storage_writes.description: Configures the amount of writes(in mega bytes) to enable logging in the persistant storage.

severity.description: Preserves logs of the specified severity and higher in  persistent storage. 'emerg'  : Preserve logs of severity 'emergency(7)' only. 'alert'  : Preserve logs of severity 'alert(6)' and 'emergency(7)' only. 'crit'   : Preserve logs of severity 'critical(5)' and above. 'err'    : Preserve logs of severity 'err(4)' and above. 'warning': Preserve logs of severity 'warning(3)' and above. 'notice' : Preserve logs of severity 'notice(2)' and above. 'info'   : Preserve logs of severity 'info(1)' and above. 'debug'  : Preserve logs of severity 'debug(0)' and above.

stop_timestamp.description: Epoch timestamp to stop logging to the persistent storage.

timeout.description: Configures the amount of time (in minutes) to enable logging in the persistant storage.

usb_target.description: URL of the USB storage to which persistent logs will be sent. URL format: 'usb:/file'.

maxsize.description: Log size (in megabytes), which would trigger rotation. 10 megabytes if not specified

period.description: The user configured period of logrotation. The possible values are 'hourly','daily','weekly'or 'monthly'. Default value is 'daily'

target.description: The user configured URI of the remote host .The valid value is 'tftp://A.B.C.D'.If not specified log files will be rotated locally.

logrotate_vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
VRF for logrotate remote host connections. If not set, then the 'default' VRF will be used. This column value can be empty.

loop_protect_disable_timer.description: This specifies the time in seconds for which the ports are to be disabled on detecting a loop. Default value is `0` i.e the port is disabled indefinitely.

loop_protect_loop_detected_trap_enable.description: Enable generating loop-protect traps when a loop is detected.

loop_protect_transmit_interval.description: This specifies the time interval in seconds between successive transmissions of loop-protect packets. Default value is `5` seconds.

macsec_selftest_enable.description: Enable MACsec selftest on this device.

memory_trap_disable.description: Disable SNMP trap generation for the memory utilization alert.

mgmd_client_details_enable.description: Enable storing of IGMP/MLD client details. This will start logging the following details: [clients_joined_count](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) in [MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) [aggregate_reports_count](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) in [MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) [aggregate_leaves_count](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) in [MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) [client_details](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) in [MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG).

mgmd_client_details_refresh_timer.description: MGMD client details refresh timer in seconds. Once the timer expires,  IGMP/MLD client details will be refreshed.

mgmd_delayed_refresh.description: Enable delayed refresh for IGMP/MLD last_reporter, debug counters and timer values. This will apply to the below attributes: [last_reporter](#/MGMD_VGS) in [MGMD_VGS](#/MGMD_VGS) [mgmd_last_reporter](#/MGMD_PGS) in [MGMD_PGS](#/MGMD_PGS) [timers_absolute](#/MGMD_PGS) in [MGMD_PGS](#/MGMD_PGS) [timers_absolute](#/MGMD_VGPS) in [MGMD_VGPS](#/MGMD_VGPS) [clients_joined_count](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) in [MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) [aggregate_reports_count](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) in [MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) [aggregate_leaves_count](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) in [MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) [client_details](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG) in [MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG](#/MGMD_VGPS_DEBUG).

mgmd_delayed_refresh_timer.description: MGMD delayed refresh timer in seconds. Once the timer expires,  IGMP/MLD last_reporter, debug counters and timer values will be refreshed.

mgmd_drop_unknown.description: MGMD Drop Unknown multicast traffic configuration.  This feature can be enabled/disabled globally or per-VLAN for IGMP and MLD.  If this field is set `on-global`, a single drop_unknown multicast filter is created to forward unknown multicast traffic for the Bridge. If this field is set as `on-vlan`, then one filter each will be created per-vlan to forward unknown multicast traffic on that VLAN.  There could be cases where even if `on-vlan` is set, there are no more multicast filters available in the switch for a vlan and the vlan would fall back to a global filter.  There could be cases where a global filter can't be supported in the given hardware platform.  In those cases, though configuration is `on-global`, per-vlan filter would be created.  There is a drop_unknown status in this same table which indicates the platform capability status.  There is a drop_unknown status at VLAN level which indicates if for that VLAN, it falls back to global filter because of filter exhaustion.  If the platform cannot support `on-global` and filters are exhausted then MGMD would flood the unknown multicast traffic on the VLAN.

mgmd_graceful_restart_interval.description: MGMD graceful restart timer in seconds. This is a common  timer for  all the active MGMD groups after daemon restart or redundancy failover.

mgmd_lookup.description: Multicast Group Membership Discovery(MGMD) forwarding lookup configuration for IGMP and MLD.  A lookup mode of `mac` indicates that the flow entries would be programmed in L2 table in hardware and a lookup mode of `ip` indicates that the flow entries woudl be programmed in L3 table in hardware.  If this field is left empty, lookup mode default is considered `mac`.  For enabling IGMPv3 and MLDv2, the lookup mode must be set as `ip`.

mgmd_querier_offload.description: Enable/Disable the IGMP and MLD Querier Offload Functionality.

mgmt_intf.description: This column is a map of string-string pairs Management interface column contains the attributes of management interface. The keys are name, mode, ip, subnet mask, default gateway, dns server IPv4 addresses. This column holds values that are configured by the user.

admin_state.description: Administrative state of the management interface.

default_gateway.description: The value for this key is default gateway IPv4 address.

default_gateway_v6.description: The value for this key is default gateway IPv6 address

dns_server_1.description: The value for this key is Primary nameserver IPv4 address.

dns_server_2.description: The value for this key is Secondary nameserver IPv4 address.

dns_server_3.description: The value for this key is tertiary nameserver IPv4 address.

ip.description: The value for this key is interface IPv4 address of the management interface.

ipv6.description: The value for this key is IPv6 address of the management interface. Possible value X:X::X:X/M.

ipv6-only-preferred.description: Enables ipv6-only-preferred option support in DHCPv4 client on the management interface.

lldp_admin_state.description: Administrative state of LLDP on the management interface.

lldp_trap_enable.description: Enables the transmission of SNMP traps for LLDP neighbor changes on the management interface.

mode.description: Determines the mechanism of obtaining IP address for the management interface.

name.description: The value for this key is a valid interface name that is to be configured as management interface

subnet_mask.description: The value for this key is subnet mask of the interface IP of management interface in CIDR format. The valid value range is 1 to 31.

mirrors.description:
Reference Resource: [Mirror](#/Mirror)
[Mirror](#/Mirror) references for sessions configured in this bridge.

mld_global_snooping.description: Enable/Disable the MLD Snooping Functionality globally.

module_trap_enable.description: Enable SNMP trap generation for Module MIB related events.

mpls_egress_clear_stats_requested.description: Number of times a request was made to clear statistics for  packets and octets/bytes transmitted with MPLS label(s).

mpls_ingress_clear_stats_requested.description: Number of times a request was made to clear statistics for  packets and octets/bytes received with MPLS label(s).

multicast_hw_activity_poll_interval.description: Poll interval in seconds to fetch the hardware activity status of multicast entries.

multicast_multipath_hash.description: Hashing algorithm to be used to decide the nexthop when multiple equal cost paths exist to reach a given source address. S-hash : This method uses only the source address to compute the hash to pick the nexthop. This is the default value S-G-hash : This method uses source and group address in the hash calculation. This is the global value applicable to all VRFs. This can be overridden per VRF.

mvrp_enable.description: Global knob to enable or disable MVRP. MVRP is enabled if the value is `True`.

nae_cli_authorization.description: Determines whether NAE agent CLI command authorization is required.

ip_address.description: Specifies the IPv4 or IPv6 address of the remote server.

password.description: The password to use when uploading the file securely. Specifies the shared secret SSH key between the client and the remote server. The transport protocol used to upload the output file. `sftp` :  Upload a file using SFTP method `scp`  :  Upload a file using SCP method

username.description: The username to use when uploading the NAE-lite action cli output file securely. Example filename: file_2024-08-26_052758_6300.txt.

disable_mac_verification.description: Disables MAC address validation on ND packets. When not set, ND packets on untrusted ports with different ICMPv6  target link layer address and packet source MAC address are dropped.

enable.description: Enables ND snooping across the system.

authentication_enable.description: Determines whether NTP Authentication is enabled in the system.

dhcp_enable.description: Disables NTP servers obtained via DHCP in the system.

enable.description: Enables NTP in the system.

ntp_config_vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
VRF for NTP connections. If this is not set then 'default' VRF will be used.

acl_log_timer.description: This key specifies the interval in seconds of the ACL logging timer.  Default value is 300 seconds.

banner.description:
Banner to be displayed on CLI start. Maximum length 4095.  Multiple lines are separated with '
'

banner_exec.description: Banner to be displayed on CLI login. Maximum length 4095.  No banner by default.

enable-statistics.description: Statistics are disabled by default to avoid overhead in the common case when statistics gathering is not useful.  Set this value to `true` to enable populating the [statistics](System.statistics) column or to `false` to explicitly disable it.

hwaddr.description: An Ethernet address in the form _xx_:_xx_:_xx_:_xx_:_xx_:_xx_ to set the hardware address of the local port and influence the datapath ID.

internal_vlan_policy.description: This key indicates order of assignment of internal VLAN ID (ascending or descending).  Default option is ascending order.

lldp_disable.description: Disables LLDP globally on the system.

lldp_hold.description: The amount of time a receiving device should hold the information sent by your device before discarding it. This variable is used as a multiplier of lldp_tx_interval, to determine the value of TTL that is carried in LLDP frames.

lldp_med_fast_start_count.description: Number of times the fast start LLDPDU should be sent during the activation of the fast start mechanism defined by LLDP-MED.

lldp_mgmt_addr_vlan_id.description: VLAN whose IPv4/IPv6 address will be advertised as the LLDP management address.

lldp_mgmt_ipv4_addr.description: LLDP Management IPv4 Address to be sent in TLV.

lldp_mgmt_ipv6_addr.description: LLDP Management IPv6 Address to be sent in TLV.

lldp_neighbor_tlv_port_lastupdate_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable updating port last update info under LLDP neighbor table or set it to `false` to disable it.

lldp_reinit.description: The amount of time in seconds to wait before performing LLDP initialization on any interface.

lldp_tlv_dot1_link_aggregation_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission of LLDP dot1 link aggregation TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting it.

lldp_tlv_mgmt_addr_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission of LLDP Management Address TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting it.

lldp_tlv_org_specific_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission/parsing of LLDP ORG TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting/parsing it.

lldp_tlv_port_desc_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission of LLDP Port Description TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting it.

lldp_tlv_port_vlan_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission of LLDP Port VLAN TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting it.

lldp_tlv_port_vlan_name_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission of LLDP VLAN Name TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting it.

lldp_tlv_sys_cap_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission of LLDP System Capabilities TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting it.

lldp_tlv_sys_desc_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission of LLDP System Description TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting it. Default is `enable`.

lldp_tlv_sys_name_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable transmission of LLDP System Name TLV or set it to `false` to disable transmitting it. Default is `enable`.

lldp_tx_interval.description: The interval in seconds at which LLDP status updates are transmitted to neighbors in seconds.

lldp_txdelay.description: The amount of time in seconds to wait before sending LLDP broadcast on any interface.

mac-aging-time.description: The maximum number of seconds to retain a MAC learning entry for which no packets have been seen.  The default is currently 300 seconds (5 minutes).  The value, if specified, is forced into a reasonable range, currently 15 to 3600 seconds.  A short MAC aging time allows a network to more quickly detect that a host is no longer connected to a switch port.  However, it also makes it more likely that packets will be flooded unnecessarily, when they are addressed to a connected host that rarely transmits packets.  To reduce the incidence of unnecessary flooding, use a MAC aging time longer than the maximum interval at which a host will ordinarily transmit packets.

mac-table-size.description: The maximum number of MAC addresses to learn.  The default is currently 16K. The value, if specified, is forced into a reasonable range, currently 10 to 256K.

mac_lockout_logging_enable.description: Enable logging of the count of packets that matched the configured lock-out MAC list and dropped.

mac_notify_enable.description: Enable the transmission of SNMP traps for MAC changes on this system (global enable).

mac_notify_interval.description: A queue mechanism is needed in this trap to throttle to amount of notifications goind out to the client at one time. The default wait time between notification being sent is 30 seconds but the user can specify an amount of time from 0-120 seconds.

snmp_agent_port.description: The port on which the SNMP agent listens for SNMP requests. The default port is 161.

snmp_historical_counters_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable the collection of historical interface statistics.

snmp_security_level.description: Enforces minimal security level for the SNMPv3 users. If  SNMPv3 user is configured not in compliance with this  provisioning, it will be operationally disabled.  'authPriv'     : users must be configured for both authentication and encryption 'authNoPriv'   : users must be configured for authentication, but privacy is optional 'noAuthNoPriv' : no restrictions on users configuration

snmpv3_engine_id.description: The SNMPv3 engine id in a colon separated hexadecimal  notation. Example 80:00:00:09:05:01:04:03:21 If not specified, local MAC will be used

stats-update-interval.description: Update interval for the statistics, in milliseconds. This option will affect the update of `statistics`, `DHCP-Relay Statistics` columns in the `Port` table, `statistics` column in the `Interface` table.  Default value is 5000 ms.

system_contact.description: This key represents the system contact.

system_description.description: This key represents the system description.

system_location.description: This key represents the system location.

tftp_server_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable TFTP server and set to `false` to disable it. If not set, TFTP server would be enabled.

tftp_server_secure.description: Set this value to `true` to enable TFTP secure mode and set to `false` to disable it. If not set, TFTP secure mode would be enabled. This config is valid only if TFTP server is enabled.

udp_bcast_forwarder_enabled.description: Set this value to `true` to enable UDP-Broadcast-Forwarder functionality globally and set it to `false` to disable it. UDP-Broadcast-Forwarder is disabled by default. If the key is missing, the configuration is assumed to be disabled. UDP-Broadcast-Forwarder port level configuration is present in [UDP_Bcast_Forwarder_Server](UDP_Bcast_Forwarder_Server).

vrrp_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable VRRP functionality globally and set it to `false` to disable it. VRRP is disabled by default.

vrrp_snmp_trap.description: Set this value to `false` to disable VRRP SNMP traps.

password_complexity.description: If password_complexity is 'enable'd, then minimal complexity rules would be enforced on all new passwords. Existing passwords are not affected.

adjacent_char_type_count.description: Enforce maximum number of adjacent character set in the new password i.e the maximum number of adjacent characters from the character set allowed in the password. The character set includes uppercase, lowercase, numeric and special characters. Default is zero(disabled)

enable.description: Enable complexity verification for new passwords.

history_count.description: Enforce minimal number of previous passwords that cannot be reused.

lowercase_count.description: Enforce minimal number of lowercase characters in the new password.

minimum_length.description: Enforce minimal length of the new passwords.

numeric_count.description: Enforce minimal number of numeric characters in the new passwords.

position_changes.description: Enforce minimal number of position changes for the new password.

special_char_count.description: Enforce minimal number of special characters in the new password.

uppercase_count.description: Enforce minimal number of uppercase characters in the new password.

poe_notification_disable.description: Disable SNMP trap generation for Power-Over-Ethernet (POE) related events.

poe_threshold.description: Set the threshold in percent at which the system will send an excess power consumption notification trap.

policy_in_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [Policy](#/Policy)
Global Policy configuration for ingress direction. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

policy_in_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'policy_in_cfg'. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'policy_in_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

cache_replace_mode.description: Replacement mode to be applied when cache limit is reached and more clients have to be added to the cache. The possible cache replace modes, are none - Specifies cache entry can't be overwritten till expiry (default) FIFO - Specifies oldest cache entry can be replaced with new entry

cache_timeout.description: The period of time in hours for which an authenticated client's information will be cached.

enable.description: Enables caching authenticated clients and their associated role information. Clients are assigned to their previously authenticated role.

persistent_storage_enable.description: Enables writing cached client information to the device's persistent storage unit.

persistent_storage_write_interval.description: Interval between consecutive cached client information writes to persistent storage file in seconds. Flash write occurs only if there is a change in cached client's information.

port_access_client_move_secure_enable.description: Enable an authenticated client to move to a new port only post a successful authentication on the new port.

port_access_client_moves_disable.description: Disable MAC move between secure ports.

port_access_event_log_client_enable.description: Enable port-access event logs for client.

port_security_enable.description: Specifies whether the port security is enabled or not  on the system. 'true': enables port security configuration globally.         Though port security is enabled globally, the         functionality is effective only if port security         is also enabled on the port. 'false': disables port security configuration on the system.

port_security_trap_disable.description: Disable SNMP trap generation for port security violations.

portaccess_auto_vlan_enable.description: Enables automatic creation of a VLAN for portaccess clients  if the VLAN is not already available in the system.

ftp.description: Specify ftp proxy configuration. Example: ftp://proxy.example.com:8080 ftp://username:password@proxy-server-address:port

http.description: Specify http proxy configuration. Example: http://proxy.example.com:8080 http://username:password@proxy-server-address:port

https.description: Specify https proxy configuration. Example: https://proxy.example.com:8080 https://username:password@proxy-server-address:port

pvlan_share_hw_resource_enable.description: Enables the Private VLAN hardware resource sharing model.

q_profile_default.description: Specifies the name of queue profile (see [name](#/Q_Profile)) for ports  that do not specify their own queue profile (see [Port](#/Port)).  When missing or when the name refers to an incomplete/invalid queue-profile,  the factory-default profile will be used (i.e. the row in [Q_Profile](#/Q_Profile)  with hw_default set true). Check the value of the queue-profile key in  [qos_status](#/System) to determine the currently operating  queue-profile.

qos_trust.description: Specifies the QoS Trust Mode for ports that do not specify their own Trust Mode (see [Port](Port) qos_config column).  `none` - no fields are inspected on arriving packets. The initial local-priority and color meta-data values are taken  from the PCP 0 entry of the PCP-to-local-priority mapping (see [QoS_COS_Map_Entry](QoS_COS_Map_Entry)).  `cos` - will use the PCP of the outermost 802.1 VLAN tag to index the  COS Map entry to initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values  of the packet. For untagged packets, the initial local-priority and color  meta-data values are taken from the PCP 0 entry of the PCP-to-local-priority  mapping. (see [QoS_COS_Map_Entry](QoS_COS_Map_Entry)).  `dscp` - will use the DSCP value of IP packets to index the DSCP Map entry to initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values of the packet.  For non-IP packets, what meta-data values are assigned is hardware dependent.  If the key is not specified, then the system will use 'none'.

qos_default.description: Specifies the schedule profile for ports that do not specify their own schedule profile (see [Port](#/Port) qos column). When missing, the [QoS](#/QoS) row with [hw_default](#/QoS) true will be used.

qos_pool_priorities_mapping_config.description:
Reference Resource: [Qos_Pool](#/Qos_Pool)
The PCP-to-lossless-pool mapping for interfaces with Priority-Based Flow Control(PFC) enabled.

radius_dynamic_authorization.description: Global configuration for RADIUS dynamic authorization feature.

enable.description: Specifies whether the Dynamic authorization is enabled.

tcp_port.description: TCP port number used by the dynamic authorization server.

udp_port.description: UDP port number used by the dynamic authorization server.

redistribute_active_routes_only.description: Enable redistributing the active routes that have been selected for forwarding into the target routing protocol.

reset.description: Resets the system when set to true.

resource_utilization_poll_disable.description: When set to *true* system resource data polling is disabled.

resource_utilization_poll_interval.description: Specifies the polling interval in seconds for system resource  data polling

access_mode.description: The REST API access mode.  read-only  - only allow read operations. read-write - allow both read and write operations.

router_id_static.description: This determines whether the system global router-ID is configured statically or selected by Routing Manager dynamically. The default value is false.

router_id_val.description: The system global router identifier. Any routing protocol may pick up this as router id, if it doesn't have a specific one configured. The router-ID may be an IPv4 address of the router. It can be any arbitrary 32bit number. However it MUST be non-zero and unique within the entire Autonomus System domain.

rpvst_enabled_vlans.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
The VLANs on which RPVST is enabled.

secure_mode.description: Will reboot, zeroize system, and set secure mode to enhanced when set to true

selftest_fail_mode.description: The selftest operation mode.   `fail-safe`  : When the mode is configured as fail-safe, the                 switch will not block interfaces post a system                 boot while selftest is in-progress. However, if                 the switch is MACsec capable and MACsec selftest                 is enabled, the MACsec capable interfaces will                 be operationally blocked until selftest is                 completes successfully on the respectiv                 interface. If selftest fails, the switch will                 continue to operate and not go down for a reboot.  `fail-secure`: When the mode is configured as fail-secure, the                 switch will keep all the interfaces on the system                 including the management interface (OOBM)                 operationally done until all the forms of                 selftest complete successfully. If any of the                 selftest fails, the switch will be automatically                 rebooted.

serviceos_password_prompt_enable.description: Specifies whether the ServiceOS password prompt is enabled or not in the system. This is only applicable for ServiceOS starting with version 01.03.0001, ignored otherwise.

snmp_communities.description: Community strings to be used by the system when communicating over SNMPv1/SNMPv2c.

aaa_server_status.description: Enable SNMP trap for AAA server status related notifications.

snmp_trap_link_status_if_mib.description: When set to true, IF-MIB trap will be sent when interface link state changes.

snmp_trap_link_status_rmon.description: When set to true, RMON trap will be sent when interface link state changes.

snmp_unique_req_id_enable.description: When set to true, SNMP unique request-id check will be enabled.

ssh_certificate_as_authkey_enable.description: When enabled, SSH will enforce that the authenticating username  is present in the authenticating certificate's Common Name,  or Subject Alternative Name User Principal Name.

ssh_ciphers.description: This option specifies the SSH ciphers to use in priority order.  The key represents the priority and the value is the cipher to  configure at that priority level. No configuration here means  that the default ciphers and priorities will be configured:   1. chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com   2. aes128-ctr   3. aes192-ctr   4. aes256-ctr   5. aes128-gcm@openssh.com   6. aes256-gcm@openssh.com

ssh_hostkey_algorithms.description: This option specifies the SSH host key algorithms that are offered  by SSH in priority order. The key represents the priority and the  value is the host key algorithm to configure at that priority  level. No configuration here means that the default host key  algorithms and priorities will be configured:   1. ecdsa-sha2-nistp256   2. ecdsa-sha2-nistp384   3. ecdsa-sha2-nistp521   4. ssh-ed25519   5. rsa-sha2-256   6. rsa-sha2-512   7. ssh-rsa

ssh_kex_algorithms.description: This option specifies the SSH key exchange algorithms to use in  priority order. The key represents the priority and the value  is the key exchange algorithm to configure at that priority  level. No configuration here means that the default key  exchange algorithms and priorities will be configured:   1.  curve25519-sha256   2.  curve25519-sha256@libssh.org   3.  ecdh-sha2-nistp256   4.  ecdh-sha2-nistp384   5.  ecdh-sha2-nistp521

ssh_login_grace_time.description: Specifies the SSH login grace time (in seconds) before a  connection being authenticated is timed out and disconnected.

ssh_macs.description: This option specifies the SSH Message Authentication Codes  (MACs) to use in priority order. The key represents the  priority and the value is the MAC to be configured at that  priority level. No configuration here means that the default  MACs and priorities will be configured:   1.  hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com   2.  hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com   3.  hmac-sha1-etm@openssh.com   4.  hmac-sha2-256   5.  hmac-sha2-512   6.  hmac-sha1

ssh_maximum_authentication_attempts.description: Specifies the maximum number of SSH authentication attemps permitted per connection.

ssh_passkeyauthentication_enable.description: Controls whether ssh password based authentication is enabled. This value will not be honored if two-factor authentication is enabled.

ssh_pubkey_algorithms.description: This option specifies the SSH public key algorithms to use in  priority order. The key represents the priority and the value  is the public key algorithm to be configured at that priority  level. No configuration here means that the default public key  algorithms and priorities will be configured:   1.  rsa-sha2-256   2.  rsa-sha2-512   3.  ssh-rsa   4.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp256   5.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp384   6.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp521   7.  ssh-ed25519   8.  x509v3-rsa2048-sha256   9.  x509v3-ssh-rsa   10. x509v3-sign-rsa   11. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256   12. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp384   13. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp521

ssh_publickeyauthentication_enable.description: Controls whether ssh public key authentication is enabled. This value will not be honored if two-factor authentication is enabled.

ssh_server_allowlist_enable.description: Controls whether the ssh server allow-list is enabled. When enabled, only configured hosts can connect to SSH servers of the switch.

ssh_server_allowlist_ips.description: Custom ssh server allow-list containing configured IPv4s and IPv6s.

ssh_server_port.description: Server port for all SSH servers on all VRFs where ssh server is  enabled.

ssh_twofactorauthentication_enable.description: This column can have one of the following settings: 'password': This means that authentication can only succeed with             successful certificate and password authentication. 'radius-authorize-only': This setting means that authentication                   will be done with a certificate followed by an                   authorization request to a RADIUS server 'disabled': Neither of the above configurations are enabled.

stp_config.description: This represents information regarding stp global configuration.

bpdu_guard_timeout.description: Time in seconds until when a port configured for BPDU-guard will be disabled upon receiving an STP BPDU. If bpdu_guard_timeout is not set, port will be in the disabled state forever.

extended_sysid_disable.description: System ID is kept as zero in the Bridge ID if this value is 'true'

forward_delay.description: The forward delay time in seconds for all the instances.

hello_time.description: The hello time in seconds for all the instances.

ignore_pvid_inconsistency_enable.description: Ignores PVID inconsistencies and allow RPVST to run on mismatched links if this value if 'true'.

max_age.description: The maximum-aging time in seconds (The time a device waits without receiving spanning tree configuration messages before attempting a reconfiguration) for all the instances.

max_hop_count.description: The maximum hop count for all the instances.

mstp_config_name.description: The MSTP configuration name configured by user. Default value is system MAC address.

mstp_config_revision.description: The MSTP configuration revision number configured by user.

path_cost_type.description: The operational value of the path cost type either long or short.

priority.description: The priority value configured as a multiple of 4096 The lower a priority value, the higher the priority.

rpvst_mstp_interconnect_vlan.description: VLAN used to interconnect an RPVST domain to an MSTP domain. This is only applicable if spanning tree is enabled on this device and the mode is set to RPVST.

stp_enable.description: Global knob to enable or disable Spanning Tree Protocol. Spanning Tree Protocol is enabled if this value is 'True'.

stp_mode.description: Spanning tree mode. The possible spanning tree modes are mstp  - Specify spanning tree to run in MSTP mode. rpvst - Specify spanning tree to run in Rapid PVST mode

tx_hold_count.description: The value used by the STP transmit state machine to limit the maximum transmission rate of BPDUs within the hello interval.

target.description: URL of the TFTP server to which supportlogs will be sent.  URL format: 'tftp://{IP|HOST}[:PORT][;blocksize=VAL]/FOLDER/'.

supportlog_rotate_vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
VRF over which the remote TFTP server (to transfer supportlogs) is to be reached. If not specified, default VRF is used. This column value can be empty.

syslog_audit_format_native.description: Enable sending audit log messages to the syslog server in Linux format. If it is not enabled, then it sends in ArubaOS-CX defined log format.

syslog_remote_facility.description: Facility to be used when forwarding to remote syslog servers.

syslog_remotes.description:
Reference Resource: [Syslog_Remote](#/Syslog_Remote)
List of syslog servers to which syslog messages will be forwarded. [Syslog_Remote](#/Syslog_Remote)

tcp_synack_retries.description: Number of times SYN-ACK packets are resent in response to a TCP  SYN request.

threshold_profile_default.description:
Reference Resource: [Threshold_Profile](#/Threshold_Profile)
Specifies the threshold-profile name for ports that do not specify their own profile (see [Port](#/Port) threshold_profile column).

timezone.description: User configured Timezone. Time zone of the device in case sensitive Posix format - "US/Pacific","Asia/Singapore", "Etc/GMT". Please refer to the full list of supported time zones at `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones`.

tls_certified_algorithms_only.description: Specifies whether TLS crypto algorithms should be restricted to  only those algorithms certified to Common Criteria NDcPP requirements.

tls_check_key_usage.description: enable the key usage check on a peer cert received during TLS handshake for client-auth or server-auth usage.

trunk_dynamic_vlan_include.description: Set to enable or disable a trunk port from automatically transmitting or receiving traffic for dynamic VLANs i.e., MVRP and PortAccess VLANs.

ubt_client_vid.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
VLAN-ID assigned to clients whose traffic is being redirected to the UBT cluster. This is not set when the UBT mode is set to VLAN-extend.

ubt_mode.description: UBT VLAN mode configuration:  `vlan-extend`: Clients are assigned to their UBT-role based                 VLAN in the hardware datapath. This mode allows                 for UBT to support VLAN-tagged clients like VOIP                 phones.  `local-vlan` : Clients are assigned to a VLAN that is local to                 the switch and associated with their UBT-role                 based VLAN when client traffic reaches the                 controller. This mode allows for reducing the                 number of VLANs that need to be instantiated on                 the switch but can only support VLAN-untagged UBT                 clients. The 'ubt_client_vid' will be used to                 specify the local_vlan that UBT clients are                 assigned to.

unicast_gr_disabled.description: The unicast_gr_disabled flag is used to indentify whether the Unicast GR feature enabled or not

usb_disable.description: Disable USB port. When disabled, devices inserted into the  USB port of the switch will not be detected and will not work.

virtual_mac.description: Global virtual MAC configuration. An example usage would be  EVPN Symmetric IRB where EVPN advertises this MAC as the Router's MAC for all the EVPN Symmetric Routes.

vlan_client_presence_detect.description: If enabled, VNI mapped VLANs will be 'UP' only if there are authenticated clients on this VLAN or have some statically configured ports as members and those ports are 'UP'. When not set, VNI mapped VLANs will always be 'UP'.

vsx.description:
Reference Resource: [VSX](#/VSX)
VSX configuration and status. If not configured, VSX functionality is disabled.

vsx_trap_enable.description: Enables sending SNMP traps for VSX events.

ztp_force_provision.description: Force ZTP based provisioning to run, ignoring the status of any previous ZTP operation.
